name: Jamalpur
tagline: The land of nakshi kantha — embroidered quilts by the hundred, the Sufi shrine that gave the town its name, and the Garo hills rising at Lauchapra on the Meghalaya border.

guide.bestTime: October to March for dry, cool weather — the best season for Lauchapra, the riverfront and the out-of-town shrines and museums.
guide.gettingThere: By road from Dhaka (~190 km, ~4–5 hr), or by rail through Jamalpur Town Junction — a junction since 1894 — with intercity trains such as the Jamuna and Tista Express. The town sits on the Old Brahmaputra; the Garo-hills spot of Lauchapra in the north is most easily reached via Sherpur.
guide.difficulty: Easy — the town sights are close together, and Melandaha, Dewanganj, Islampur and Bakshiganj are day trips by bus, train or CNG.

mustVisit.name: Shrine of Hazrat Shah Jamal (RA)
mustVisit.description: The shrine of the Sufi saint who gave the town and district their name — a quiet place of devotion near the Old Brahmaputra in Jamalpur Sadar.
mustVisit.history: Tradition holds that Hazrat Shah Jamal came to this region centuries ago to spread Islam; the settlement, once called Singhjani, took the name Jamalpur from him. His mazar remains a focus of local veneration.

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: In Jamalpur town, near the Old Brahmaputra

tips: Dress modestly and be respectful — it is an active place of devotion
Pair it with the Doyamoyee Mandir and the riverfront in town

mustVisit.name: Doyamoyee Mandir
mustVisit.description: An old Hindu temple complex near the heart of Jamalpur town, with shrines to Shiva and Kali and a pillared nat-mandir — one of the district's most enduring pieces of heritage.
mustVisit.history: Commonly said to be around three centuries old (with a founding sometimes dated to the late 17th century), the Doyamoyee temple has long been a centre of worship and festival in the town.

practical.hours: Daylight hours; busiest at Hindu festivals

mustVisit.bestTime: Daytime; festival days for the atmosphere
tips: Be respectful and quiet — it is an active temple
Look for the nat-mandir and the older brick shrines

mustVisit.name: Lauchapra Picnic Spot
mustVisit.description: Jamalpur's only hill country — a green eco-spot on the Garo Hills border with India's Meghalaya, with watch-towers, a lake and forest, where the plains rise suddenly into hills.
mustVisit.history: Developed by the Zila Parishad as a picnic and eco-tourism spot in the far north of Bakshiganj upazila, Lauchapra looks straight across to the Garo Hills and the homeland of the Garo communities of the borderlands.

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: Far north in Bakshiganj upazila, ~10 km beyond Bakshiganj sadar
howToReach.transport: Bus/CNG via Bakshiganj (road access is often easiest via Sherpur)

tips: It is a border zone — carry ID and follow any local guidance
Go early to make the most of the day and the light on the hills

mustVisit.name: Gandhi Ashram & Freedom Struggle Museum
mustVisit.description: A Gandhian ashram on the bank of the Jhinai River in Melandaha, carrying on self-reliance and handicraft work, with a museum of the freedom struggle.
mustVisit.history: Founded in 1934 by Nasir Uddin Sarkar to spread Gandhi's message of non-violence and self-reliance, the ashram became a hub of khadi and rural craft; a Freedom Struggle Museum was added in 2007.

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: Melandaha upazila, on the Jhinai River, ~15 km from town

tips: Allow time for the museum and the riverside grounds
A good window into the district's craft and freedom-struggle history

mustVisit.name: Zeal Bangla Sugar Mills
mustVisit.description: One of the oldest sugar mills in the country, at Dewanganj — its tall chimneys and crushing season a piece of living industrial heritage on the northern plains.
mustVisit.history: Established in 1957 (originally as Zeal Pak Sugar Mills, renamed after independence), the mill has milled cane through the decades and remains a landmark of the district's industrial past and present.

practical.hours: An operating industrial site — view from the public approach

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: Dewanganj upazila, north-west of Jamalpur town

mustVisit.bestTime: Crushing season (winter) for the mill at work
tips: It is a working factory — do not enter restricted areas
Best appreciated for the heritage architecture from outside

mustVisit.name: Old Brahmaputra Riverfront
mustVisit.description: The wide, slow Old Brahmaputra runs along Jamalpur town — an easy riverside walk at the ghats, with boats, fishers and big open skies.
mustVisit.history: Jamalpur sits on the Old Brahmaputra, once the river's main course; after the great earthquake of 1762 the Brahmaputra's flow shifted west to form the Jamuna, leaving this gentler channel along the town.

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: Along the edge of Jamalpur town
howToReach.transport: Walk or rickshaw to the ghats

mustVisit.bestTime: Late afternoon for the light on the water
tips: Sunset over the river is the moment to wait for
Country-boat rides can sometimes be arranged at the ghats

specialties.name: Jamalpur Nakshi Kantha
specialties.description: Jamalpur is the country's premier centre for nakshi kantha — quilts hand-embroidered with folk motifs by thousands of women across the district. 'Jamalpur Nakshikantha' was granted a Geographical Indication (GI) tag in 2024, and the town's craft market runs to hundreds of shops.
specialties.venue: Nakshi kantha shops and craft villages, Jamalpur town

specialties.name: Local Festive Sweets
specialties.description: Jamalpur kitchens are known for festive and wedding sweets such as chhana polao and para sandesh, made by the town's confectioners.

bucketlist.title: Buy a Jamalpur nakshi kantha
bucketlist.detail: An embroidered quilt from the country's nakshi-kantha capital — a craft so identified with the district it earned a GI tag in 2024.

bucketlist.title: Reach the Garo hills at Lauchapra
bucketlist.detail: The district's only hill country, on the Meghalaya border — watch-towers, lake and forest with the Garo Hills rising across the line.

bucketlist.title: Visit the shrine of Shah Jamal
bucketlist.detail: The Sufi saint's mazar that gave the town its name, near the Old Brahmaputra.

bucketlist.title: See the Doyamoyee Mandir
bucketlist.detail: An old town temple complex with Shiva and Kali shrines and a pillared nat-mandir, reckoned around three centuries old.

bucketlist.title: Walk the Gandhi Ashram at Melandaha
bucketlist.detail: A 1934 Gandhian ashram on the Jhinai River, with a Freedom Struggle Museum and a long tradition of khadi and craft.

bucketlist.title: Watch sunset on the Old Brahmaputra
bucketlist.detail: The wide, slow river along the town glows at golden hour — once the Brahmaputra's main course before 1762.

bucketlist.title: See Zeal Bangla Sugar Mills
bucketlist.detail: One of the oldest sugar mills in the country (1957) at Dewanganj — industrial heritage and a winter crushing season.

bucketlist.title: Arrive by train at Jamalpur Junction
bucketlist.detail: A railway junction since 1894 — the classic way to reach the district from Dhaka.

bucketlist.title: Visit the shrine of Shah Kamal
bucketlist.detail: The mazar of Hazrat Shah Kamal at Durmut in Islampur, a place of local pilgrimage north-west of town.

bucketlist.title: Taste chhana polao and para sandesh
bucketlist.detail: The town's festive and wedding sweets, made by Jamalpur's confectioners.

bucketlist.title: Watch nakshi kantha being stitched
bucketlist.detail: Across the district's craft villages, women embroider folk motifs into quilts by hand — the work behind the GI tag.

bucketlist.title: Eat fresh river fish
bucketlist.detail: Fish from the Old Brahmaputra and the Jamuna, fried fresh or in light curries at riverside eateries.

foods.name: Chhana Polao
foods.description: A festive sweet of fresh chhana (curd cheese), a Jamalpur wedding and celebration favourite.

foods.name: Para Sandesh
foods.description: A local sandesh prepared by the town's confectioners, eaten at festivals and as gifts.

foods.name: Old Brahmaputra River Fish
foods.description: Freshwater fish from the Old Brahmaputra and the Jamuna — fried fresh or in light curries.

foods.name: Khejur Gur
foods.description: Date-palm jaggery from the winter harvest, used in the season's pithas and sweets.

famousPeople.name: Amjad Hossain
famousPeople.knownFor: Acclaimed film director, writer, lyricist and actor born in Jamalpur; director of classics such as Golapi Ekhon Train-e and Bhat De, and recipient of the Ekushey Padak.

famousPeople.name: Abdullah Al Mamun
famousPeople.knownFor: Pioneering playwright, theatre director and actor born at Amla Para in Jamalpur Sadar — a major figure of modern Bangladeshi theatre, honoured with the Bangla Academy Award and Ekushey Padak.

didYouKnow: The town and district are named after the Sufi saint Hazrat Shah Jamal, whose shrine stands in Jamalpur Sadar; the area was earlier known as Singhjani.
Jamalpur is the government-designated 'Land of Nakshi Kantha', and 'Jamalpur Nakshikantha' was granted a Geographical Indication tag in 2024.
Jamalpur town sits on the Old Brahmaputra — the Brahmaputra's main flow shifted west to form the Jamuna after the great earthquake of 1762.
Lauchapra in Bakshiganj sits right on the Garo Hills border with India's Meghalaya — the district's only stretch of hill country.
Zeal Bangla Sugar Mills at Dewanganj, founded in 1957, is one of the oldest sugar mills in the country, and Jamalpur Town Junction has been a railway junction since 1894.
